details:
Project Name: Space Academy – Interactive Space Exploration Simulator

Space Academy is an interactive, browser-based educational game designed to introduce users to the challenges of astronaut training, space exploration, and mission management. The project allows players to take on the role of an astronaut, select or customize their character, complete preparation exercises, and perform preflight Go/No-Go safety checks before beginning a lunar mission.

During the mission, players must manage essential resources, including oxygen, power, food, fuel, radiation shielding, and crew morale. They face unexpected situations such as solar storms, oxygen leaks, space debris, temperature problems, and communication difficulties. Players must make decisions, complete interactive challenges, and balance their resources to keep the mission running successfully. The game also includes a lunar landing sequence that tests the player's ability to control the spacecraft and achieve a safe landing.

The main benefit of this project is its educational approach to space science. Instead of simply presenting scientific information, it allows users to explore concepts through interactive gameplay. It introduces topics such as microgravity, astronaut health, lunar dust, solar activity, radiation protection, space debris, and communication delays. Its scientific facts are inspired by NASA research and educational resources.

The intended impact is to make learning about space more engaging and accessible, encourage scientific curiosity, and help users understand the importance of planning, teamwork, resource management, and decision-making in space missions.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML was used to structure the game, CSS to create its visual design and responsive interface, and JavaScript to implement the gameplay, character customization, resource management, interactive challenges, random mission events, and landing mechanics. The project runs in a web browser and does not require specialized hardware.

The creative aspect of Space Academy is the combination of educational science content with simulation and game-based learning. Players do not just read about astronaut responsibilities; they experience simplified versions of mission preparation, problem-solving, and resource management themselves. The astronaut selection and customization features, space-themed interface, interactive mini-games, and dynamic mission events make the experience more engaging.

During development, important factors included scientific accuracy, educational value, ease of use, accessibility, engaging gameplay, and realistic mission challenges. Resource balance and the consequences of player decisions were also considered so that users could understand how different systems depend on one another. NASA educational resources were used as references for the scientific information presented in the game.
